chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Abu al-Mi'za, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) granted concession to women and children to rush (from Mina to Muzdalifah) at night, and to throw the Jamarat at night, and to pray the morning prayer in their homes; so if they feared menstruation, they would go to Mecca and appoint someone to offer the sacrificial animal on their behalf.
ai.seo_question: What are the concessions for women and children during Hajj regarding night rush, Jamarat, and prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Prophetic principle of *rukhas* (concessions) in Hajj, specifically easing the burden on women and children who are exempt from the strict requirement of spending the night in Muzdalifah. It permits them to perform the stoning of the Jamarat and the dawn prayer from their tents in Mina, with the option to return to Mecca if they fear menstruation, thereby reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on flexibility and ease (*taysir*) in ritual obligations for those with valid excuses.
